what_it_is.prose: India's Active Protection System (APS) for main battle tanks is an indigenous programme led by DRDO to develop a combined soft-kill and hard-kill system capable of protecting armoured vehicles against incoming anti-tank guided missiles (ATGMs) and rocket-propelled grenades (RPGs). The system draws on concepts from the Russian ARENA APS and the Israeli Trophy APS, but is being developed as an indigenous solution tailored to Indian operational requirements. The hard-kill component uses explosive countermeasure projectiles to physically intercept and destroy incoming threats within seconds of detection, while the soft-kill component employs IR jamming and smoke grenade dischargers to defeat laser-guided and infrared-guided missiles. The APS is intended for integration on the T-90S Bhishma and Arjun Mk-1A main battle tanks, significantly enhancing their survivability against the growing proliferation of advanced ATGMs on the battlefield. The programme is in the procurement phase, with the Indian Army evaluating the system for fleet-wide integration.

faq.question: What is an Active Protection System (APS)?
faq.answer: An Active Protection System (APS) is a vehicle-mounted defensive system that detects and defeats incoming anti-tank threats (ATGMs, RPGs) before they strike the vehicle. APS systems have two components: soft-kill (IR jamming, smoke) to defeat guided missiles, and hard-kill (explosive countermeasures) to physically intercept and destroy incoming projectiles. APS significantly enhances tank survivability on the modern battlefield where advanced ATGMs are proliferating.

faq.question: Is India developing an indigenous APS or buying foreign systems?
faq.answer: India is developing an indigenous APS through DRDO, drawing on concepts from the Russian ARENA and Israeli Trophy systems. The indigenous system is tailored to Indian requirements and intended for the T-90S and Arjun Mk-1A fleets. Whether the Israeli Trophy system is also being considered for procurement alongside the indigenous solution has not been publicly confirmed.

faq.question: Why is an active protection system (APS) critical for India's tank fleet?
faq.answer: India's T-90 and T-72 tanks face modern anti-tank guided missiles (ATGMs), top-attack weapons and kamikaze drones that can defeat passive armour. An APS detects and intercepts incoming threats, giving the fleet a survivability upgrade that reactive armour alone cannot provide.

faq.question: How is India procuring this active protection system?
faq.answer: The Defence Acquisition Council has approved a capital acquisition programme for an Indian Army active protection system, and global firms are being invited to bid against an indigenous option. The programme is being run as a competitive tendering exercise, with Indian industry participation encouraged.
